A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DoAug research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, diversity, affinity, ablation, sensitivity, and model-architecture experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds human validation, metric comparisons, DPO-replacement experiments, and reasoning and multilingual evaluations.

M1.justification: Both versions use supervised paraphraser training, Euclidean-distance preferences, DPO, selective coreset augmentation, and distance-based output selection. Newly explained adapter merging does not establish a procedural change. Algorithm 1 corrects S_select to S_retain, matching the procedure already described in v1 Section 3.4.

E1.justification: The twelve English classification datasets remain. v2 Appendix M adds CSQA and CODAH multiple-choice reasoning tasks and Twitter sentiment evaluation in English, Spanish, German, French, Italian, and Portuguese. These substantially extend task and language coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds AEDA to the main and GPT-2/T5 comparisons, Code-Mixed to the new multilingual experiment, and temperature/prompt alternatives in the DPO-replacement study. The original eleven baselines remain. Llama-based implementations of AugGPT and other prompting baselines were already disclosed in v1 Appendix C.

E3.justification: v2 adds unique 3-grams, excludes invalid words from lexical diversity, and changes Table 2 from average ranks to normalized-score averages. New protocols include human evaluation of 200 samples per dataset and metric comparison on 1,000 sources with 5,000 paraphrases. The low-resource comparison revises reported counts from 600 original plus 600 augmented samples to 800 plus 400, and pruning-ratio labels change. These revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds experiments testing whether higher temperature or diversity prompts can replace DPO, and examines Euclidean-versus-cosine selection agreement, correlation, and distributions in Appendices G–H. Human paraphrase-validity checks and lexical ablation results also expand the analyses. Existing generation-count, coreset, architecture, and low-resource studies largely remain.

E5.justification: Both Table 1 captions report means and standard deviations over ten random seeds. v2 Appendix D newly specifies that methods use matching seeds, while Appendix C reiterates the run count. Appendix G also introduces Pearson correlation estimation for the metric comparison. No increase in repeated runs or new confidence intervals is reported.

E6.justification: Retained accuracy entries in Tables 1 and 4 are unchanged, with AEDA results added. Table 3 corrects DoAug's Yelp accuracy from 59.67 to 56.57. Raw diversity results change, including DoAug distance from 9.5308 to 9.6430, alongside revised evaluation reporting. New findings include 95% human-assessed validity, metric correlation of 0.96, and DPO-replacement, reasoning, and multilingual results. These additions do not demonstrate a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds the mathematical definition of the newly evaluated unique-3-gram measure, 3-gram(S) = |G3|. The optimization formulation, LoRA/DPO equations, and existing diversity and affinity formulas remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims: diversity-oriented paraphrasing with DPO and coreset selection improves diversity while preserving coherence and downstream performance. The headline 10.52% average gain remains. Additional supporting experiments and the sixth diversity metric do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 develops new interpretations of component roles: sampling chiefly affects latent diversity, while DPO affects lexical diversity, and fine-tuning is argued necessary relative to cheaper alternatives. It adds metric-choice rationale and default coreset recommendations. Limitations now acknowledge restricted reasoning and multilingual coverage, human/model evaluation biases, and the exclusion of Arabic, replacing several statements that these evaluations were absent.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code link, dataset access locations, the exact paraphrasing prompt, adapter-training/merging details, and the 20,000-source-by-five-paraphrase composition of SFT data. Appendix D newly explains baseline sample selection and matching of dataset sizes. Most learning rates, epochs, hardware, software versions, and training times were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for CSQA, CODAH, multilingual benchmarks, and additional AI/LLM applications. The related-work discussion and positioning against existing augmentation methods remain substantially unchanged. Publication updates for works such as LoRA, back-translation, and CCS are bibliographic changes rather than new prior art.

P1.justification: v2 divides experimental settings into numbered subsections, relocates metric formulas to Appendix A, expands dataset and implementation explanations, and reorganizes the appendices. It also adds acknowledgments and corresponding-author identification. Most introductory, methodological, and concluding prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a conceptual illustration and several analytical and benchmark figures, expands diversity displays to six metrics, and separates normalized and raw diversity tables. Existing plots are rearranged, pruning axes and mislabeled architecture-comparison metrics are corrected, and appendix plots are compressed. The original framework diagram is retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central diversity-and-coherence argument: human checks supplement LLM-only judgments, replacement controls test the need for DPO, and reasoning/multilingual experiments address v1's narrow evaluation scope. Added prompt, adapter, baseline-sampling, and access details improve reproducibility. Some new protocols remain underspecified, and Appendix K retains a stale 'twice the size' statement after correcting sample counts, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the stronger validation and transparency.
